minutes.headline: Board approved three Holman Street entertainment licenses and deferred the budget and capital plan articles.
minutes.summary: Only three of four board members attended. They appointed a reserve police officer and an ADA committee member, approved a gasoline storage license, and approved the Holman Street entertainment licenses after long public comment. They discussed the town manager evaluation process with labor counsel and argued over the proposed HR director/assistant town manager and recreation positions. They then went through the warrant articles, supporting many and deferring the budget, capital plan and others.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved three one-day entertainment licenses for Holman Street, with conditions and a 250-person maximum, after long public comment.
The board deferred recommendations on the budget, capital plan, salary plan and other articles; no recommendation prints unless it is unanimous.
The board supported the transfer to the special purpose stabilization account and the OPEB trust transfer, and voted to support article 1.
The board signed the 2019 annual town meeting warrant and the annual town election warrant.
Only three of four members attended; the board also appointed a reserve police officer and approved a gasoline and diesel storage license.

why_it_matters: The budget and capital plan articles that set next year's tax bill went to the warrant without a Select Board recommendation, so voters at Town Meeting will decide them without one.
The Holman Street licenses were decided separately from any zoning question, so neighbors' concerns about events there may return through other town processes.
watch_next: Public meeting on the town manager evaluation on May 7.
Whether the board settles its recommendations on the deferred articles before Town Meeting.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main licenses, the appointments, Article 1 and the warrant signings, but the official minutes record many more votes, including recommendations on Articles 2, 9 and 11-37. The thing to check is the Article 9 and Article 10 amounts, which ours garbles ($100,000 vs $200,000), along with the Articles 26-31 result and the land acquisition committee nomination, which only ours records.
